links.comparator_used: Models trained without demographic balancing (implied unbalanced baseline; the abstract does not state it explicitly), across 7 architectures and 6 gender- or race-targeting balancing strategies
links.outcome: Cross-axis fairness (AUC, TPR, Brier score) on non-targeted demographic axis in one-year mortality prediction
links.effect: Gender-targeting largely preserved race fairness; race-targeting consistently disrupted gender fairness across all methods and most architectures. No numeric values reported in abstract.
links.tradeoff: Race-targeting incurred greater performance costs and calibration loss; fairness gains may reflect leveling down rather than genuine improvement; the same intervention could look successful under TPR but fail under AUC.
links.quote: Gender-targeting interventions largely preserved race fairness, while race-targeting consistently disrupted gender fairness across all methods and the majority of architectures.

design_hint: demographic balancing with cross-axis fairness auditing
